title: G4: straightforward-goal route, zero scouts by default, five-file limit as a warning, read scope and interface contracts in specs, one-line Planner reminder
spec:
Documentation and skill changes only; no Python. The analysis: routine changes should incur less orchestration; default to zero scouts and spawn one only for a named uncertainty whose answer could change the implementation; treat the five-file limit as a warning threshold and split by independently verifiable behaviour and dependency boundaries; parallel workers need explicit interface contracts even when file scopes do not overlap; keep the Planner reminder short so prompt prefixes stay cacheable.
Change:
1. .claude/skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md: replace the scout fan-out step with a routing table by goal type: clear localized change -> brief spec, one executor, deterministic gates, human PR; uncertain location or behaviour -> one targeted investigation (a scout with a named uncertainty written into plan.md), then spec; independent changes -> separate workers with an explicit interface contract in each spec; high-risk or architectural -> detailed planning, spec review, execution, independent review. Default zero scouts; the Planner greps for what it needs first. The five-file limit becomes 'warn above five; split by verifiable behaviour, never to satisfy the count'.
2. .claude/skills/write-spec/SKILL.md: spec fields gain read_scope (paths a worker may inspect, listed so the packet can include them), interface_contract (functions, signatures, file formats other tasks rely on), task_class (mechanical, unfamiliar, debugging, architectural, security; feeds executor routing) and route (straightforward or full); acceptance stays mandatory.
3. CLAUDE.md (repo): rule 3 'Fan out 3–6 narrow scouts' becomes the zero-scout default with the named-uncertainty exception; rule 5 keeps atomic specs but states the warning semantics of the file limit; add the routing table pointer.
4. .claude/hooks/planner-prompt.sh: the per-message reminder becomes one line ('Planner mode: goals go through Skill(orchestrate); never edit source; see CLAUDE.md') so the changing part of every prompt is short; the enforcement stays in planner-mode.sh.
5. README: a 'Routes' subsection in Pipeline with the table.
Acceptance is by content: grep the files for the new sections; no tests to add beyond the existing hook tests staying green.
acceptance: orchestrate/SKILL.md contains the four-row routing table and the words 'zero scouts'
write-spec/SKILL.md documents read_scope, interface_contract, task_class and route
CLAUDE.md no longer says 'Fan out 3–6 narrow scouts' and states the warning semantics for the five-file limit
planner-prompt.sh emits one line and the existing hook tests pass
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree
